description: getff turns a project's conventions into executable gates in its native toolchain — custom ESLint rules and git hooks for npm projects, clippy for cargo — so a violated convention fails at the earliest reachable channel instead of in CI. This repository is the framework itself; its installer wires that enforcement layer into a consumer project.
rules: Start at README.md#why-this-exists for the project goal, then .claude/session-bootstrap.md for the reading order; a doc that contradicts README has drifted.
Read .claude/rules/00-rule-index.md first — it is the generated digest of every discipline rule; the authoritative text of each rule lives in .claude/rules/<name>.md.
Enforce every convention at the earliest reachable channel (edit-time, pre-commit, pre-push, then CI); treat CI as the last-resort gate, never the first.
Never let human or AI attention be the detection layer of a load-bearing check — see .claude/rules/attention-is-not-a-mechanism.md.

Before adding a capability, consult docs/meta-factory/prior-art-evaluations.md and carry a Prior-art: commit trailer; CLAUDE.md section "Build-vs-reuse invariant" defines what counts as a capability commit, and .claude/rules/build-first-reuse-default.md holds the macro-level discipline.
Never call a paid LLM from CI — see .claude/rules/no-paid-llm-in-ci.md.
Pin every tool install in a workflow to an exact version — see .claude/rules/ci-tool-pinning.md.
Give every doc one authoritative scope and state what it is NOT authoritative for — see .claude/rules/doc-authority-hierarchy.md.
Customise a getff-installed artefact through a sibling <file>.override.md, never by editing the shipped file in place — see INSTALL-FOR-AI.md.
